knowledge_point.title: Rewriting a Double Integral Over a Circle or Part-Circle Not Centered at the Origin

question.:question/problem:
Let $D=\{(x,y):x^{2}+(y+\frac{3}{2})^{2}\leq\frac{9}{4},\ x\leq0\}$. Rewrite

$$
\iint_D \ln{\left(x^{2} + y^{2} + 1 \right)}\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

Select the polar-coordinate setup whose bounds cover $D$ once with $r\geq0$ and whose integrand includes the area factor. Do not evaluate the integral.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use $x=r\cos\theta$, $y=r\sin\theta$, and $\mathrm{d}A=r\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$. The full disk has radius $\frac{3}{2}$ and center $(0,- \frac{3}{2})$.

**Radial bounds.** Expanding the disk inequality gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x^2+y^2+3y&\leq0\\r^2+3r\sin{\left(\theta \right)}&\leq0\\r(r-(- 3 \sin{\left(\theta \right)}))&\leq0.\end{aligned}
$$

For $r>0$, divide by $r$; the origin is included as well. Thus $0\leq r\leq - 3 \sin{\left(\theta \right)}$.

**Angular bounds.** The upper radial bound must be nonnegative. The full disk permits $\pi\leq\theta\leq2 \pi$. Intersect this sweep with $x\leq0$, or $r\cos\theta\leq0$. Choose $\pi\leq\theta\leq\frac{3 \pi}{2}$. Every interior point is covered once.

![Region, representative radial segment and angular sweep](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/edb-math/repairs/2026-10-29-matrix-outer-fences/generator-probes/17592186129275-hard/fc8ead294cae14190f3a.png)

**Transformed integrand.** Use $\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta=1$. The density substitution and area factor give

$$
\begin{aligned}\ln{\left(x^{2} + y^{2} + 1 \right)}&=\ln{\left(r^{2} \sin^{2}{\left(\theta \right)} + r^{2} \cos^{2}{\left(\theta \right)} + 1 \right)}\\&=\ln{\left(r^{2} + 1 \right)}\\\ln{\left(x^{2} + y^{2} + 1 \right)}\,\mathrm{d}A&=r \ln{\left(r^{2} + 1 \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore the required setup is

$$
\displaystyle\int_{\pi}^{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}\int_{0}^{- 3 \sin{\left(\theta \right)}}r \ln{\left(r^{2} + 1 \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta.
$$

**Other choices.** $\displaystyle\int_{\pi}^{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}\int_{0}^{- 3 \sin{\left(\theta \right)}}\ln{\left(r^{2} + 1 \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$: The area factor is missing. $\displaystyle\int_{\pi}^{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}\int_{0}^{\frac{3}{2}}\ln{\left(r^{2} + 1 \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$: The center-to-boundary radius is incorrectly used as a constant polar upper bound. The area factor is missing. $\displaystyle\int_{- \frac{\pi}{2}}^{0}\int_{0}^{3 \cos{\left(\theta \right)}}r \ln{\left(r^{2} + 1 \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$: These bounds describe a different disk or part-disk, with a different center direction. $\displaystyle\int_{- \frac{\pi}{2}}^{0}\int_{0}^{3 \cos{\left(\theta \right)}}r^{2} \ln{\left(r^{2} + 1 \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$: These bounds describe a different disk or part-disk, with a different center direction. The area factor was squared instead of used once.

question.:question/problem:
Let $D=\{(x,y):x^{2}+(y+1)^{2}\leq1,\ x\geq0\}$. Rewrite

$$
\iint_D x^{2} + y^{2}\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

Select the polar-coordinate setup whose bounds cover $D$ once with $r\geq0$ and whose integrand includes the area factor. Do not evaluate the integral.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use $x=r\cos\theta$, $y=r\sin\theta$, and $\mathrm{d}A=r\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$. The full disk has radius $1$ and center $(0,-1)$.

**Radial bounds.** Expanding the disk inequality gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x^2+y^2+2y&\leq0\\r^2+2r\sin{\left(\theta \right)}&\leq0\\r(r-(- 2 \sin{\left(\theta \right)}))&\leq0.\end{aligned}
$$

For $r>0$, divide by $r$; the origin is included as well. Thus $0\leq r\leq - 2 \sin{\left(\theta \right)}$.

**Angular bounds.** The upper radial bound must be nonnegative. The full disk permits $\pi\leq\theta\leq2 \pi$. Intersect this sweep with $x\geq0$, or $r\cos\theta\geq0$. Choose $\frac{3 \pi}{2}\leq\theta\leq2 \pi$. Every interior point is covered once.

![Region, representative radial segment and angular sweep](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/edb-math/repairs/2026-10-29-matrix-outer-fences/generator-probes/17592186129275-hard/680793990000f961fec9.png)

**Transformed integrand.** Use $\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta=1$. The density substitution and area factor give

$$
\begin{aligned}x^{2} + y^{2}&=r^{2} \sin^{2}{\left(\theta \right)} + r^{2} \cos^{2}{\left(\theta \right)}\\&=r^{2}\\x^{2} + y^{2}\,\mathrm{d}A&=r^{3}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore the required setup is

$$
\displaystyle\int_{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}^{2 \pi}\int_{0}^{- 2 \sin{\left(\theta \right)}}r^{3}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta.
$$

**Other choices.** $\displaystyle\int_{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}^{2 \pi}\int_{0}^{- 2 \sin{\left(\theta \right)}}r^{4}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$: The area factor was squared instead of used once. $\displaystyle\int_{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}^{2 \pi}\int_{0}^{1}r^{2}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$: The center-to-boundary radius is incorrectly used as a constant polar upper bound. The area factor is missing. $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\int_{0}^{2 \cos{\left(\theta \right)}}r^{3}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$: These bounds describe a different disk or part-disk, with a different center direction. $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\int_{0}^{2 \cos{\left(\theta \right)}}r^{2}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$: These bounds describe a different disk or part-disk, with a different center direction. The area factor is missing.

question.:question/problem:
Let $D=\{(x,y):x^{2}+(y-3)^{2}\leq9,\ x\geq0\}$. Rewrite

$$
\iint_D x y^{2}\,\mathrm{d}A.
$$

Select the polar-coordinate setup whose bounds cover $D$ once with $r\geq0$ and whose integrand includes the area factor. Do not evaluate the integral.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use $x=r\cos\theta$, $y=r\sin\theta$, and $\mathrm{d}A=r\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$. The full disk has radius $3$ and center $(0,3)$.

**Radial bounds.** Expanding the disk inequality gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x^2+y^2-6y&\leq0\\r^2-6r\sin{\left(\theta \right)}&\leq0\\r(r-(6 \sin{\left(\theta \right)}))&\leq0.\end{aligned}
$$

For $r>0$, divide by $r$; the origin is included as well. Thus $0\leq r\leq 6 \sin{\left(\theta \right)}$.

**Angular bounds.** The upper radial bound must be nonnegative. The full disk permits $0\leq\theta\leq\pi$. Intersect this sweep with $x\geq0$, or $r\cos\theta\geq0$. Choose $0\leq\theta\leq\frac{\pi}{2}$. Every interior point is covered once.

![Region, representative radial segment and angular sweep](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/edb-math/repairs/2026-10-29-matrix-outer-fences/generator-probes/17592186129275-hard/d3e3c47f83568e38d2f9.png)

**Transformed integrand.** The density substitution and area factor give

$$
\begin{aligned}x y^{2}&=r^{3} \sin^{2}{\left(\theta \right)} \cos{\left(\theta \right)}\\x y^{2}\,\mathrm{d}A&=r^{4} \sin^{2}{\left(\theta \right)} \cos{\left(\theta \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore the required setup is

$$
\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\int_{0}^{6 \sin{\left(\theta \right)}}r^{4} \sin^{2}{\left(\theta \right)} \cos{\left(\theta \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta.
$$

**Other choices.** $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\int_{0}^{6 \sin{\left(\theta \right)}}r^{2} \sin^{2}{\left(\theta \right)} \cos{\left(\theta \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$: The area factor was divided out instead of multiplied in. $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\int_{0}^{3}r^{2} \sin^{2}{\left(\theta \right)} \cos{\left(\theta \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$: The center-to-boundary radius is incorrectly used as a constant polar upper bound. The area factor was divided out instead of multiplied in. $\displaystyle\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}\int_{0}^{- 6 \cos{\left(\theta \right)}}r^{4} \sin^{2}{\left(\theta \right)} \cos{\left(\theta \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$: These bounds describe a different disk or part-disk, with a different center direction. $\displaystyle\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}\int_{0}^{- 6 \cos{\left(\theta \right)}}r^{3} \sin^{2}{\left(\theta \right)} \cos{\left(\theta \right)}\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta$: These bounds describe a different disk or part-disk, with a different center direction. The area factor is missing.
